title: Heat totals and averages
scenario: Neralis Meltworks is checking 24 fictitious EAF heats from its Kestrel plant. The superintendent needs total output, average tap time and one pooled metal-yield result. Every mass is in metric tonnes; each row is one heat.

lesson.intro: A formula starts with =. A range such as Data!D2:D25 includes both endpoints. Build totals and means from cells so the result follows the data, instead of typing a calculated answer.

functions.name: SUM
functions.arguments: number1 is a number, cell or range; later arguments are optional additional inputs.
functions.mistake: Exclude headings and unrelated numeric columns; text in referenced cells is ignored.

functions.name: AVERAGE
functions.arguments: number1 supplies the first number or range; optional inputs add more observations.
functions.useCase: Typical tap time or measured mass.
functions.mistake: Referenced blanks are ignored, but zero is included. An average of individual yields differs from pooled yield.

lesson.combine: For pooled yield, divide total tapped mass by total charged mass and multiply by 100. Arithmetic operators * and / combine results. The ratio of totals weights larger heats correctly. Use Data! before ranges when entering formulas on Answers.

tasks.prompt: Calculate the total tapped mass for all 24 heats, in metric tonnes.
Calculate the average tap duration for all 24 heats, in minutes. Submit the unrounded numeric value.
Calculate pooled metal yield as 100 times total tapped mass divided by total charged mass. Submit the unrounded percentage number, for example 93.4 rather than 0.934.
Calculate the difference between average charged mass and average tapped mass, in tonnes. Submit an unrounded number.

bonus.prompt: Calculate aggregate tapped tonnes per hour using total tap duration, rather than averaging individual heat rates.

columns.name: Tap_date
columns.description: ISO date of tap in September 2026.
